THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING ON INTERLOCUTORY  APPLICATION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:6359  MFA No. 104159 of 2017  JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for hearing on interlocutory application, with the consent of the learned counsel for parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the claimant/injured seeking enhancement of compensation, being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 09.03.2012 passed in MVC.No.2279/2010 by the Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court-IV & MACT., Belgaum (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.
Heard Sri. Deepak S.Kulkarni, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant and Sri.
M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant submits that the Tribunal has committed grave error in not awarding any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
He submits that the appellant is also entitled to an NC: 2024:KHC-D:6359 enhanced compensation on all the other heads.
Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal.

5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the appellant has sustained minor nasal bone fracture, since, there cannot be any functional disability, therefore, the Tribunal is justified in not awarding any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
He submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal on all the other heads is also just and proper, which does not call for any enhancement.
Thus, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6. I have heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Meticulously perused the material available on record.
The appellant/claimant examined himself as PW1 and also examined one Doctor namely Sri.S.R.Angadi as PW2 in support of his claim petition.

PW2 in his evidence deposed that the Shri. Shivyogi Basavanneppa Neelagund vs Shri. Shivanand Shivalingappa Angadi on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8328765/

sentences.text: appellant has sustained fracture of right and left nasal bone fracture and he is facing difficulty in breathing, however, the said statement is not supported with any evidence on record to come to a conclusion that the appellant is facing difficulty in breathing.
Mere sustaining fracture to the nasal bone cannot be termed as a disability.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly denied the compensation under the head of future income due to disability.
8. This Court taking note of the injuries suffered by the appellant and considering the material available on record, reassesses the compensation on the following heads:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:6359 Particulars Amount (in Rs.)

Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 Food, nourishment, special diet, 15,000/-
conveyance and attendant charges Loss of income during laid-up-period 16,500/-
 Medical expenses 3,000/-
 Total 1,04,500/-

Thus, the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,04,500/- as against Rs.72,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

9. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,04,500/- as against Rs.72,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount of shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per NC: 2024:KHC-D:6359 annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.

d) The respondent No.2/Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the claimant/injured.
